rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;
rows.note: This counts every row in the Track table, treating each track as part of the catalog.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar."Name", COUNT(al."AlbumId") AS album_count
FROM "Artist" ar
JOIN "Album" al ON al."ArtistId" = ar."ArtistId"
GROUP BY ar."ArtistId", ar."Name"
ORDER BY album_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed ties are resolved arbitrarily, so only one artist is returned.
I counted all customers, including those with a NULL country, grouped under a NULL row.

rows.sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, SUM(Total) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Invoice
GROUP BY Year
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I assumed revenue is the sum of the Invoice.Total column, grouped by the calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
       ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent
FROM Customer c
JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
LIMIT 5;
rows.note: I assumed "amount spent" means the sum of invoice totals per customer.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount
FROM Customer c
JOIN Employee e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "support rep" means the employee linked to customers through `Customer.SupportRepId`.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Playlist p
JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
rows.note: I assumed "Grunge" is the exact name of a playlist in the Playlist table. If no playlist has that name, the count returns 0.
I assumed "purchased" means the track appears in at least one invoice line.

rows.sql:
SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue
FROM Invoice
WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01'
GROUP BY BillingCountry
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed revenue means the sum of invoice totals grouped by billing country for calendar year 2012.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name
FROM Artist ar
JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: I assumed a track's artist is the artist of its album, and I excluded tracks with no genre.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note:
Revenue per genre can be computed from InvoiceLine (UnitPrice × Quantity) joined to Track and Genre, then divided by the overall total.



I assumed revenue means line-item UnitPrice × Quantity, and tracks with no genre are excluded.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
      SELECT i2.CustomerId
      FROM Invoice i2
      JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
      JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
      JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
      WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: I assumed genres are identified by the Genre table's Name column, with "Rock" and "Jazz" matched exactly.

rows.sql:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS MonthNumber,
       SUM(Total) AS Revenue
FROM Invoice
WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011'
GROUP BY MonthNumber
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "invoice revenue" means the sum of the Total column for invoices dated in 2011.

Discontinued is stored as TEXT ('0' or '1' in the sample data), so I compare it to '1'.



I assumed a value of '1' marks a discontinued product.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';

SELECT c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount
FROM Categories c
JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName
ORDER BY ProductCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "most products" means the count of products linked to each category via Products.CategoryID.

rows.sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS OrderYear, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY OrderYear
ORDER BY OrderYear;
rows.note: I assumed the year should be taken from the OrderDate column.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AverageFreight
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName;
rows.note: I assumed "shipper" refers to the shipping company linked to each order via ShipVia.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName
FROM Employees e
JOIN Employees m ON e.ReportsTo = m.EmployeeID
WHERE m.FirstName = 'Andrew' AND m.LastName = 'Fuller';
rows.note:
Andrew Fuller is EmployeeID 2 (from the sample rows), and employees link to their manager via ReportsTo.



I assumed Andrew Fuller's ID is found by name rather than hardcoded, so the query works even if the ID differs.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders o
JOIN Employees e ON o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "handled" means the employee recorded on the order (Orders.EmployeeID), and that ties are broken arbitrarily.
I assumed "average product unit price" means the average of UnitPrice across all rows in the Products table.
I assumed "shipped to" refers to the ShipCountry column on Orders, not the customer's country.

rows.sql:
SELECT p.ProductName,
       ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue
FROM "Order Details" od
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;
rows.note: Revenue is calculated as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from the Order Details table.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice
FROM Products p
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE p.UnitPrice = (
    SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice)
    FROM Products p2
    WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
ORDER BY c.CategoryName;
rows.note: I assumed "most expensive" means the highest UnitPrice in the Products table, and ties would show every product at that max price.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CompanyName,
       SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
FROM Orders o
JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed revenue means UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from the order line items, and that "in 2021" refers to OrderDate.

rows.sql:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM Orders
WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021'
GROUP BY month_number
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "orders in a month" means counting rows in `Orders` by `OrderDate`.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders o
JOIN Employees e ON o.EmployeeID = e.EmployeeID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '1997'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "handled" means the employee recorded on the order, counted by the order date's year.
